summary: Compose qualified Telegram photo, album and MP4-video publication through the released-upload worker bridge.

impacts.evidence: Media scope is derived from the host-owned connector account and released-upload gate.
Media bytes remain in the upload storage boundary and are not copied to canonical events or audit.
The existing provider-neutral SocialPublishRequest and worker dispatch are reused.
No event envelope or event payload changes.
The existing SocialPublisher and MediaAccessor interfaces are reused.
Existing upload release records, social publication state and receipts are reused.
Multipart requests are bounded and released-upload access is revalidated immediately before opening content.
The existing social publication lifecycle and connector capability settings remain mandatory.
Existing publication and receipt lineage covers the media write without storing media contents.
Telegram has no caller idempotency key; existing receipt recovery handles ambiguous media writes.
The host Telegram transport adds bounded multipart egress under the existing fixed-host policy.
Existing worker leases, retry/DLQ, request timeout and Telegram rate policy remain active.
Disabling media/video capability admission or upload processing stops new media publication without migration.
Deterministic multipart, mapping, adapter and runtime tests cover success and malformed media cases.
